title: Runbook Atomizer & Safe Replay Engine for Incremental Ops Tasks
creator: Avery Chen
summary: Break monolithic runbooks into small, idempotent task units (atoms) and build a Safe Replay Engine to execute, simulate, and audit sequences with permissioned gating and dry-run semantics.
motivation: Oncall engineers and first-line support waste time navigating long, procedural runbooks. We want to reduce human error, make partial automation safer, and enable incremental automation rollouts (canary internal, then wider). Atomic tasks allow retries, partial progress, and better telemetry to reduce MTTR and unlock auto-remediation later.
background: Existing runbooks are largely free-text steps or long scripted playbooks. Several recent incidents showed repeated manual mistakes when operators copied/pasted sequences. Prior work (runbook fragments and typed runlets) partially extracted steps, but there is no single execution model, permission model, or safe replay capability across the operator surface.
design_proposal: 1) Define an 'Atom' contract: typed inputs, explicit side-effects, idempotency hint, pre-check and rollback hooks. 2) Build an Atom registry and metadata store (immutable versions). 3) Implement Safe Replay Engine: simulate -> dry-run -> gated-execute with RBAC and signed approval. 4) Provide a lightweight UI/CLI to sequence atoms into 'sessions' and persist transcripts to the runbook audit log. 5) Telemetry: token/time/cost per atom, success/failure category, operator actions during replay.
tradeoffs:
- Storing granular atoms increases metadata surface and catalog operational cost.
- Strict idempotency requirements may make some steps harder to author; we will provide helper libraries.
- Early rollout will need manual review for high-risk atoms (DB migrations, infra changes), delaying automation benefits.
- Complexity vs. benefit: aim for high-signal first with a small atom set (10-15) covering common fixes.

acceptance_criteria: Atoms can be registered and versioned; registry rejects mutable updates to published versions
Engine supports simulate and dry-run that produce deterministic transcripts without side-effects
RBAC gating enforces approval for atoms tagged high-risk and stores approvals in audit log
Telemetry captures atom-level latency, success/failure, operator overrides, and cost estimates
CLI can compose a session of >=5 atoms and replay in simulate/dry-run/execute modes
Documented roll-forward and rollback guidance for each atom exists in the registry

rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal alpha (oncall + SRE) with simulate/dry-run only. Phase 1: gated execute for low-risk atoms (ops-only). Phase 2: canary auto-remediate for a small subset with monitoring and automatic rollback. Phase 3: broad rollout and developer-facing atom creation templates.
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit structured events for atom.register, atom.version.publish, session.start, session.simulate_end, session.execute_start, atom.execute.result. Build a Grafana dashboard showing top failing atoms, median execution latency, operator override rate, and correlation with MTTR. Alert if operator_override_rate > 15% for 6h or if simulate->execute mismatch > 2%.
qa_notes: Create fuzz tests for atom inputs, property-based tests for idempotency hints, and a suite of replay determinism tests. Validate simulate output matches dry-run transcripts in >99% of cases. Runbook authors should write a 'safety spec' per atom describing preconditions and invariants.
docs_and_playbooks: Add 'Atom Authoring Guide' to the docs site, templates for pre-check hooks, and a sample 'session' representing a common PG restart scenario. Link these docs from the registry UI and include a checklist for security review.
